clue.text: The mockery of a carrier without underwear

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the carrier's letters go round the underwear

parts.note: a tray is something for carrying plates and cups
a vest is an undergarment in British usage

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a delivery person who has turned up with no underwear on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here is the old sense of outside, not lacking. In Britain a vest is an undershirt, not a waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque, absurd imitation, a parody that makes something look ridiculous.

clue.text: A Mongol seamen's get-together

indicators.note: a get-together of seamen means two sailors placed side by side

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor; the plural asks for more than one

explanation.surface: A Mongol warrior is invited to a sailors' party.
explanation.walkthrough: Two seamen, each a TAR, meet up side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tartars were a Turkic people of the Mongol hordes, so a Tartar is loosely used for a Mongol.

clue.text: Could be mad with rage — or love

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged into something else, so they are shuffled

parts.note: ire is a literary word for anger or rage

explanation.surface: Being furious and being in love are said to be close cousins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' tells you to rearrange MAD plus IRE (rage); 'with' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire someone is to regard them with warm approval, a kind of affection.

clue.text: Birds to be seen in the wilderness

indicators.note: the letters can be seen sitting inside the word wilderness

explanation.surface: A birdwatching note about species found out in the wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernes are sea eagles, large birds of prey.

clue.text: No-one's to catch up. That would cause stress

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the whole run of letters is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
one is I, a Roman numeral, and the 's stands for is
a net is used to catch fish

explanation.surface: A warning that if nobody keeps pace, the strain will tell.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'No-one's' disguises a split into no, one (I, the Roman numeral) and is; 'up' turns the whole string backwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Tension is strain or pressure, the very thing that produces stress in a person or a material.

clue.text: Hear the poet was shut out

indicators.note: hear signals that a word is to be said out loud and matched by sound

parts.note: the Bard is Shakespeare, the poet par excellence

explanation.surface: A poet is told he has been refused entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the poet' is BARD, Shakespeare's nickname; spoken aloud it matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone barred from a place is excluded or kept out of it.

clue.text: Meant to transform the exterior of some home

indicators.note: the reworked letters form the outside, with the other piece inside them
to transform the letters is to change their order

parts.note: part means some, as in some of the cake

explanation.surface: An instruction to remodel the outside of a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to transform' rearranges MEANT into AMENT, which forms 'the exterior of' PART: A-PART-MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An apartment is a flat, a self-contained dwelling, so a home.

clue.text: Recital involving a member of the family

definitions.meaning: a recital is a telling or narration of events
a relative, such as an aunt or cousin

explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' simply links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a narrated account of events and a kinsman connected by blood or marriage.

clue.text: Section in a legal document which has to be left

indicators.note: in places the section inside the legal document

parts.note: a deed is a signed legal document, such as one transferring property
a part is a section of something

explanation.surface: A lawyer notes a clause in a contract that must be removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' does the placing; 'which has to be' is padding that leads into the definition, read as the past participle 'left'.
explanation.definitionFit: Departed means gone away, having left; 'left' is read as a past participle.

clue.text: Thinking that's incongruous in a social worker

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or peculiar
taken as written
the ant is a social insect, and its workers do the colony's labour

explanation.surface: Someone finds it odd to see deep thought from a welfare officer.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'social worker' here is an insect: ants live in colonies with worker castes. RUM is British for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruminant can mean contemplative, given to meditation, just as cows chew over their cud.

clue.text: Hit the drink!

definitions.meaning: to strike hard, a heavy blow
British slang for beer or ale

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an order to start drinking heavily; WALLOP is old British slang for beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a hard punch and, in British slang, mild beer or ale.

clue.text: Monster duck, almost entirely grey

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: almost entirely means the word is used except for its final letter

explanation.surface: A drab, nearly all-grey waterbird described as a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' is not the bird but cricket's zero, O; 'almost entirely' drops the last letter of grey.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of fairy tales, a monster.

clue.text: A call to keep others from striking

indicators.note: the call holds the others inside it, keeping them

parts.note: to ring someone is to phone or call them
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: A phone call meant to stop workers going on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' looks like industrial action, chiming with 'keep others from', but it is the definition, meaning eye-catching; 'to keep' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Arresting means attention-grabbing, impressive, catching the eye.

clue.text: Coach tour arranged about the end of August

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the other piece
arranged signals that the letters are put in a new order
the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A coach trip planned for late summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' suggests a bus, but it is the definition, a teacher. 'arranged' gives TUOR from tour, placed 'about' T, the last letter of August.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor coaches a pupil, giving private instruction.

clue.text: Shock due to the head's backing

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: nut is slang for the head, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: Someone is shaken after the headteacher supports them.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'head' is not a headteacher but slang for the skull, NUT; NUT'S read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to daze or stupefy, as a sudden shock does.

clue.text: The opposition leader gets on his feet and offers conjectures

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to rise is to stand up

explanation.surface: In Parliament the head of the opposition stands up to speculate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opposition leader' looks like a politician, but it gives only O, the first letter of opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: To theorise is to form hypotheses, putting forward speculations.

clue.text: Looks on a metal container as an obnoxious thing

parts.note: eyes means looks at, as in eyes someone up
ore is rock that contains metal

explanation.surface: Gazing at a tin canister and finding it hideous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a metal container' suggests a tin, but ore is the rock that holds metal. 'on' simply puts EYES before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is an ugly, unpleasant sight, something offensive to look at.

clue.text: An individual working for awfully poor rate

indicators.note: awfully signals that the letters are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone toils for a miserably low wage.
explanation.definitionFit: An operator is a person who works a machine or runs a business.

clue.text: Truly conned, though far from ill-informed

parts.note: well means truly or thoroughly, as in well aware
to con is an old word for to study or read carefully

explanation.surface: A clever person was genuinely tricked even though they knew a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conned' looks like swindled but is the old verb con, to study.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well-read has studied widely, so is knowledgeable rather than ignorant.

clue.text: Before opening make check!

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before
a vent is an opening for air or smoke

explanation.surface: An instruction to inspect something before launching it.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevent is to stop or hinder, the sense of check as a verb.

clue.text: Thanks to a politician, one will have to stop up

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A grateful constituent says a politician will block something.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British for thanks; MP is a Member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: To tamp is to pack something down firmly, as clay is rammed in to seal a blasting hole.

clue.text: Carry a little child — there's point to that

parts.note: a tot is a toddler
E for east is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Lifting a toddler, a parent remarks that there is purpose to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' is a compass point, here E for east.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to carry or lug something around.

clue.text: There's rent trouble. Blow!

parts.note: rent as an adjective means ripped, torn apart
ado means fuss or bother

explanation.surface: A tenant's exasperated cry over a dispute about the rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like money paid to a landlord, but it is the past of rend, torn; a 'blow' is a gale.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent windstorm, and a blow is a storm of wind.

clue.text: Campanologist with a double?

definitions.meaning: a bell-..., someone who practises the art of bell-ringing
a lookalike, as in a dead ... for someone

explanation.walkthrough: 'with' only links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person who rings church bells and a person who closely resembles another.

clue.text: Such a muscle can take no rest

indicators.note: the letters can take a different shape, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A muscle that is never allowed to relax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can take' tells you the letters of NO REST take on a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A tensor is a muscle that tightens or stretches a body part.

clue.text: The chief is straight as can be

definitions.meaning: a leader or sovereign who governs
a measuring stick is the model of a straight line

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is playful: a measuring rule is about as straight as anything can be.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a sovereign who governs and a straight-edged measuring strip.

clue.text: Fish filling used by sea-borne soldier, spread on bread

indicators.note: the fish fills the soldier, going inside him

parts.note: a marine is a soldier serving at sea
a gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A fish sandwich made by a navy soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling' signals the container. A gar, or garfish, is a needle-nosed fish often met in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Margarine is a butter substitute, spread on bread.

clue.text: Equally determined to gain an advantage

parts.note: as means equally, as in as good
set means determined, resolved, as in set on winning

explanation.surface: Equally resolved to get ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful or valuable quality, a benefit.

clue.text: He believes he is included among the abstemious

indicators.note: the words are placed inside, included among the other letters

parts.note: TT means teetotal, so abstaining from alcohol
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man of faith says he is one of the teetotallers.
explanation.walkthrough: TT stands for teetotal; HE IS goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A theist is someone who believes in God.

clue.text: Wise people will accept America's food

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: sages are wise people
America's gives USA

explanation.surface: Wise people take to American cuisine.
explanation.walkthrough: US goes inside SAGES.
explanation.definitionFit: Sausages are a food, minced meat in a casing.

clue.text: Getting an artist to serve up salad-stuff

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
to dish up is to serve food

explanation.surface: Asking an artist to prepare a salad.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a Royal Academician, is the stock crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A radish is a crunchy root vegetable used in salads.

clue.text: Toiler going off with some hesitation to become an idler

indicators.note: going off means going wrong, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitating in speech

explanation.surface: A hard worker falters and turns lazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going off' turns the surface's hard worker into a dawdler: the anagram gives LOITER, and the sound of hesitation follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A loiterer hangs about aimlessly, an idler.
